JM Financial Limited has informed the Exchange about earnings conference call on Monday, November 6, 2023 at 11:00 a.m. (IST) to discuss the Company s financial performance for the second quarter and half year ended September 30, 2023.

Guidance & outlook: On the financial numbers for Q1 FY27, net revenue increased by 13% Y-o- Y to INR883 crores, and pre-provision operating profit increased by 21%.
We closed 9 Ca pital Markets transact ions aggregating to approximately INR22,000 crores in Q1 FY27.
For Q1 FY27, net revenue for the segment stood at INR115 crores as against INR182 crores and PAT stood at INR32 crores.
Growth & demand: Even if you were to exclude those two large IPOs, we've seen a decent growth, and the pipeline is at INR150,000 crores.
On our Affordable Housing business, it reported a strong Y-o-Y growth in disbursements of 87% and a 28% Y-o-Y growth in AUM.
Wealth loan book grew by 43% year-on-year to INR2,417 crores and recurring AUM of our wealth business grew to approximately INR33,400 crores.
Margins & costs: Pre-provision operating profit increased by 21% year-on-year to INR469 crores, and PAT (ex-provisions) before minorities increased by 24% Y-o-Y to INR379 crores.
Net revenue for Q1 FY27 doubled to INR462 crores and pre-provision operating profit grew almost 2.3x to INR375 crores.
Our margin trade financing book 5 years ago was less than INR400 crores.
Capex & expansion: We're expecting very good numbers in most of these funds and we continue to invest in the Asset Management business.
So our investment in the INR12,000 crores is INR3,114 crores.
And my last question would be on that you had rightly emphasized continued investment in Wealth Management and Asset Management.
Balance sheet & cash: In Private Markets, we witnessed one of the best quarters for our Asset Reconstruction business with very strong resolutions in distressed credit assets during the quarter, where we collected over INR2,000 crores and the group share of that cash flow was over INR1,200 crores.
Gross resolutions were over INR2,000 crores, of which group share of cash flows was over INR1,200 crores.
7 years back, we were at peak debt to equity of almost 3x in the ARC, and we will be debt-free.
Risks & challenges: In Wealth Management, performance was a little subdued because of weak transactional business, which is again related to the markets and also the primary market issuance, but the recurring AUM and loans have shown good traction.
Despite the subdued markets, they are at 15% ROE for last quarter.
But again, as I said, even market conditions being weak, the business has generated 15% return on equity.

Guidance & outlook: We had guided INR250 crores to INR300 crores of recovery in each of the years FY26, '27 and '28, we've achieved over INR270 crores in FY26, and we seem to be pretty much on target to be between the INR250 crores and INR300 crores number for FY27.
We closed 41 capital markets transactions aggregating to approximately INR95,000 crores in FY26.
On a year -on-year basis, net revenue for FY26 increased by 11% to approximately INR789 crores and operating profit after tax increased to INR347 crores.
Growth & demand: Last 2 years, the revenue growth in this business has been close to 17%, and the profit growth has been over 40%.
Affordable home loans, we've seen a very strong growth in AUM to almost INR3,500 crores now and a revenue growth of 37% in the last 2 years.
Operating profit before tax for FY26 grew 3.5x to INR742 crores and operating profit after tax after minority interest grew almost 3.6x to INR543 crores.
Margins & costs: And we've seen our operating profit before tax grow from INR328 crores to INR452 crores and a healthy margin of 48%.
Operating profit after tax adjusted for such impact stood at INR1,133 crores, which is a year-on-year increase of 38%.

It means are we working on some marginal costing principle or because whatever the company and employee are earning the same amount, INR100 crores, INR100 crores, our PAT has grown by INR100 crores and employee cost also increased by INR100 crores.
Capex & expansion: And despite escalated geopolitical tensions and market volatility, our total fees, commission and brokerage business, which CACM is a large part of and so is Wealth Management, has seen a decent 10% year-on-year growth as well to almost INR1,753 crores.
On physical expansion on a year -on-year basis, branches have increased by 10 to 72 branches and franchisees have increased to 874.
50% of that business is fees, commission and interests and 50% is roughly broking and others.
Balance sheet & cash: Over the last 4 quarters, an aggregate of approximately INR5.95 per share of dividend has been paid or proposed, resulting in a distribution of approximately INR570 crores as dividend.
And we are comm itted to declaring 50% of that PAT as dividend every year for our shareholders.
And therefore, literally in the last 14 months, we have declared INR570 crores of dividend to our shareholders, and this is a significant amount.
Risks & challenges: There is a little bit of volatility in the markets that we continue to see, which was there in Q4 and Q1 of this financial year as well and until the FPI selling continues, it's becoming increasingly difficult to get IPOs done.
